text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-Donors at the Washington "Friends of Lebanon" conference announced over $3 billion aid to Lebanon's reconstruction.
-Gross foreign exchange reserves of the central bank rose in the first half of December by $12.43 million to $5.779 billion.
-Lebanon's weekly treasury bill issue of December 12 raised 323.1 billion Lebanese pounds, with a nominal surplus of subscription against maturity of 138 billion pounds.
-Parliament Speaker Berri to chair the children's parliament on Wednesday.
-Prosecutor general demanded death penalty for 21 people charged with dealing with Israel.
-The cost of roads rehabilitation in Lebanon is estimated at $1.25 billion, Minister of Public Works Harajli said.
-Sibline's cement company signed a $57.5 million syndicated loan with six banks to finance expansion plans.
-A five-nation ceasefire monitoring committee discussed an Israeli complaint following Katyusha rocketing of its northern borders.
-Hizbollah said two guerrillas were killed in a weekend attack against Israeli troops inside Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone.
